subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename workspace files as part of the core bootstrap context contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but broadening startup context injection changes a trusted prompt/file-loading boundary and may create a new public hook contract.

options.title: Approve Guarded Custom Files
options.body: Allow explicit in-workspace custom basenames through the existing hook path once the linked PR or a replacement is repaired, documented, and tested against path guards and budgets.

options.title: Keep Recognized Basenames Only
options.body: Decline arbitrary workspace-file injection and direct users to first-class workspace filenames or documented conventions instead.

options.title: Defer To Broader Context Design
options.body: Supersede this issue with a larger context API decision if maintainers do not want raw configured files to be the permanent contract.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Custom Files
recommendation.body: Allow explicit in-workspace custom basenames through the existing hook path once the linked PR or a replacement is repaired, documented, and tested against path guards and budgets.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest available routing owner for the boundary and product/API decision around bootstrap file injection.
